title: Exploitation of Security Vulnerability on Retirement
problem: The processor's retirement unit, which retires micro-operations in order from the Reorder Buffer, experiences stalls based on the first instruction's execution time. Since retirement is shared between logical cores on the same physical core, attackers can observe retirement availability to deduce instructions executing on co-located logical cores.
motivation: Identifying new microarchitectural side-channels exposes processor security vulnerabilities and enables development of stronger defenses.
method: The attack observes the retirement unit—the part of the processor that finalizes instructions in order—to detect stalls (delays) when instructions are slow. Because this retirement unit is shared between two logical cores (lightweight threads sharing one CPU core), one program can watch the other program's retirement activity to infer what it's doing. The researchers create two covert channels by manipulating retirement stalls: one uses different instructions to encode messages, another uses the same instructions in different quantities. They extend this to launch a Spectre v1 attack (where the CPU guesses incorrectly which instruction to run next, enabling secret extraction) and develop a program identification attack that recognizes victim programs based on their unique retirement usage patterns.
key_novelty: Exploiting the shared retirement unit between logical cores—the component that completes instructions in order—reveals a microarchitectural side-channel (information leakage through CPU internal mechanics) that enables covert communication and victim program identification.
contributions: Two novel covert channels bypassing existing protection strategies
New Spectre v1 variant leveraging retirement and misprediction behavior
Program inference attack using retirement usage patterns

metrics.other: Attack feasibility and ability to bypass existing protections demonstrated

primary_theme: Microarchitectural side-channel exploitation through processor retirement
